Class HttpResponse.BodyHandlers

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.jdk.net.http.HttpResponse.BodyHandlers
Enclosing interface:
HttpResponse<T>
public static final class HttpResponse.BodyHandlers extends Object
The available HttpResponse.BodyHandlers. Each one is created once, in its own class, so a program links only the handlers it asks for: one that only reads bytes carries none of the String code.

  • Method Details

    • ofByteArray

      public static HttpResponse.BodyHandler<byte[]> ofByteArray()
      Delivers the body as bytes. Returns the same handler every time, so calling it in a loop allocates nothing.

    • ofString

      public static HttpResponse.BodyHandler<String> ofString()
      Delivers the body as a String of every byte received, so body().length() is the size received, with no limit but the free memory. A body with a Content-Length is allocated once, at that size; one without it (a chunked body) grows as it arrives. A body that does not fit in the free memory fails the request with an IOException rather than stopping the program. The bytes are not decoded: a runtime String holds bytes, so UTF-8 text stays UTF-8, and a NUL byte ends it. Returns the same handler every time; each response allocates its String.
